chunks: 1984 - And in the narration of Rifa‘ah ibn Musa, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about a man who comes during the month of Ramadan from a journey, such that he expects he will enter upon his family in the mid-morning or later in the day.
He said: 'If dawn rises while he is outside and has not yet entered, then he has the choice: if he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break the fast.'

key_terms.أَفْطَرَ: he broke the fast, meaning he may choose not to fast
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn, the decisive time marker for the ruling
key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: having the choice or option between two permitted courses
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: journey or travel, the condition affecting the fasting ruling
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time in which the fasting ruling is being discussed
key_terms.صَامَ: he fasted, meaning he may choose to observe the fast

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who returns home during Ramadan after dawn?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a traveler returning in Ramadan after dawn while still outside his hometown. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام states that in such a case, the person has the option either to fast or to break the fast that day. It is a jurisprudential narration concerning fasting during travel and return from travel.
